answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent stakes tokens that are slashed if it misbehaves, so a raven flock of cheap clones cannot flood the market without paying real cost. Like a cedar that grows slowly and deep, trust accrues only through sustained honest work, while a nebula of throwaway accounts stays thin and untrusted. Attackers face simple math: each new identity costs money, and honest history cannot be bought overnight.
